text:
sec-bot: [ALERT] credential-finder flagged a PGP private key-looking blob in gs://redwood-ci/artifacts/build-2026/pgp-key.asc.gz (kms wrapped). tagging @eng-security :rotating_light:
alice: saw the alert. grabbing the artifact now. anyone changed build scripts this week?
bob: I pushed a runner image update last night but didn't touch upload steps. pulling and inspecting.
carla: can you paste a sanitized header (no private material) so we can confirm if it's a private key?
bob: fetched, sanitized: ```-----BEGIN PGP PRIVATE KEY BLOCK----- (truncated) -----END PGP PRIVATE KEY BLOCK-----``` 'looks like a full private key'
alice: ouch. object metadata shows kmsKeyName: projects/redwood/locations/global/keyRings/builds/cryptoKeys/wrap-key — that's our CI wrap-key. darren, can you confirm KMS bindings?
darren: checking now. found two principals with decrypter: svc-ci-runner@redwood.iam.gserviceaccount.com (expected) and svc-legacy-bridge@redwood.iam.gserviceaccount.com (unexpected). hold on removal.
carla: triage list: 1) copy artifact to secure evidence bucket + delete public copy (alice) 2) rotate/wrap-key create new version & update CI refs (bob/darren) 3) enumerate recent artifacts for PGP blocks (sec-bot analytics) 4) audit IAM binding for decrypter and remove unexpected principals (darren) 5) collect KMS usage audit logs for 60 days (audit-team)
bob: I'll do the key version rotation and update CI env var KMS ref. proposed steps:
```
# create new key version
gcloud kms keys versions create --key=wrap-key --location=global --keyring=builds
# update CI config to point to projects/redwood/locations/global/keyRings/builds/cryptoKeys/wrap-key/versions/<new>
# redeploy runners with limited SA
```
darren: removed legacy binding `svc-legacy-bridge@redwood.iam.gserviceaccount.com` and opened follow-up to verify it's not used. change is in audit logs.
alice: copied evidence to gs://redwood-sec-evidence/build-2026/pgp-key.asc.gz (access: audit-only). original removed from gs://redwood-ci/artifacts/build-2026/. DM me if you need access.
sec-bot: evidence snapshot created and analytics scan queued. found 6 other artifacts containing PGP-like blocks in the last 21 days; flagged for manual review.
carla: opened quick PR to lock down bindings and add an audit hook. tagging @audit-team for the log export.
audit-team: scheduling ingestion of cloudkms.cryptoKeyVersion.useToEncrypt and useToDecrypt events for builds key and any runner wrap keys for last 60 days.
alice: starting inventory of repos and pipelines that reference this GPG key id (searching for key fingerprint / ascii header). need product/security input on signing keys to rotate.
bob: CI infra PR: https://github.com/redwood-ci/infra/pull/499 — updates KMS refs and reduces SA scope; deploy planned in 20m.
darren: created incident INC-2026-142, severity medium, tracking rotation and downstream impact on signing.
carla: compliance note: we must bundle audit logs, evidence copies, and the rotation timeline for legal review. I'll collect once audit logs land.
alice: sec follow-ups: 1) full creds sweep across artifacts (sec-bot), 2) rotate any discovered signing keys, 3) validate no external exposure/usage of leaked key. escalate if used.
bob: deployed updated runners and new KMS version reference. monitoring for CI failures.
darren: IAM cleanup done; recorded in audit: https://console.cloud.audit/logs/entry/iam-change/xxxxx
sec-bot: analytics review queued; manual review owners assigned.
carla: good triage. next check-in 40m. if anyone finds signs of key being used publicly (git commits, package signatures), escalate to incident commander immediately. thanks team :thumbsup:
